speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked	the Minister for Transport with regard to the 26 defective MRT trains (a) whether the defects being not "safety-critical" meant that they pose zero safety risks for commuters; (b) why is it most effective for the car-bodies to be entirely replaced when cracks have been found only on the bolsters; (c) what are the risks for cracks to happen on other components of the car-body; and (d) whether the monthly safety assessment is focused only on the found defects or conducted for the entire train.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: What it means is that the bolsters are able to take more than three times the maximum stress that they may experience during operations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The cracks have not reduced this safety margin.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In other words, all these can be tested in the laboratory and you can check it out that, despite having the cracks, the safety margin of at least three is still being preserved.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In any case, as I said just now, LTA, SMRT and Kawasaki-Sifang continue to monitor closely the affected trains, including those that have been repaired and returned to service.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Other parts of the trains are not affected.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What is the difference between the bolsters being made in Japan versus those being made in China?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Why is the decision now for the bolsters to be made in Japan rather than in China?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is there a confidence issue with manufacturing of train parts in China and, if it is so, is Ministry going to take this into account for future contracts?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They said, "Well, since it is defective, I will replace your bolsters".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And they offered to now use a Japanese bolster and, of course, we said "You are welcome to use Japanese bolsters".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In fact, the first generation of Kawasaki trains all used Japanese bolsters.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I do not think we need to read anything more into this.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I do not want to create a diplomatic problem.
